### Added
- **Workflow notifications that reach nobody are now named.** "No valid
  recipients were identified for this notification" is one of the more common
  automation errors, and nothing in HubSpot tells you which workflow caused it.
  HubScan now reads the recipient configuration on every enabled workflow's
  internal email and in-app notifications, and reports the ones that can no
  longer reach anyone: a named user who has been deactivated or removed from the
  portal, or a team with no members left. Each finding names the workflow, the
  action and the reason, so it is a fix rather than a hunt. Verified live on a
  reference EU1 Enterprise portal: 38 notification actions across 102 enabled
  workflows, and no false positives.
- **Notifications addressed to a record owner get a blast radius.** A workflow
  that notifies "the deal owner" reaches nobody for a deal with no owner, or one
  whose owner has been deactivated. The report now pairs those workflows with the
  record counts the data-quality pillar already measures, so you can see how many
  records notify no one before deciding whether it matters.

### Fixed
- **`probe` no longer looks like it contradicts itself about workflows.** The
  workflow check read one flow but phrased it as a portal count, so it could
  report "0 enabled" directly above a line reporting ten. It now reads the same
  page as the check below it, and says so when a portal has more than one page.

### Changed
- **One extra read scope on the Service Key: `settings.users.teams.read`.** Team
  membership is a separate grant from the user list, the same way `automation`
  is separate from `automation.sequences.read`. Without it HubScan cannot tell an
  empty team apart from one it simply could not read, so it stays quiet rather
  than guessing. The token guide and quick start now list all 16 scopes, and
  `probe` checks the new one like every other.
